evidence: submit(): passes payload fields to this.payroll.submitHours and returns { id: sheet.id }. It only delegates and maps the response.
approve(): calls this.payroll.approve and returns { approved: sheet.approved }. Any approval rules live in the business layer.
export(): calls this.payroll.run(week) and formats the result with the presentation view payslipRow joined by newlines. This is presentation formatting.
HoursPayload interface: a request DTO, which belongs in presentation.
audit.log calls are delegated to PayrollAuditService (business). The controller only chooses when to call it and applies no logic of its own.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: PayrollController is a thin presentation handler, which fits its layer. It defines the transport payload shape (HoursPayload), hands each operation to the business services (PayrollService.submitHours, approve, run) and builds the response objects. The export output is formatted by the presentation view helper payslipRow. The file has no persistence, SQL, storage or framework-infrastructure logic, and no business rules such as pay calculation, hours validation or approval rules. One borderline point: the controller itself makes the audit.log calls after submit and approve. That is a small amount of application-level coordination, but it goes through a business service and contains no decision logic, so it does not move a business rule into the presentation layer.
